text: dsh-remote-control 是面向 DSH Web 客户端的远程访问插件：它在网页侧边栏提供控制面板，由主机连接用户配置的 relay，并通过隧道转发 DSH 自带的网页客户端。面板可配置 relay 地址和共享密钥，启停连接、生成配对链接和二维码、复制链接、查看连接状态并运行连接测试。适合需要从手机或其他浏览器继续访问这台 DSH 主机的用户；需要自行配置 relay 服务和对应密钥。

dsh-remote-control lets you reach a DSH host's web client from another browser through a relay. Its sidebar sets the relay and shared secret, starts or stops the host link, creates pairing links, shows status, and runs a connection test. Configure your own relay and secret.
想从手机浏览器远程打开家里运行的 DSH。
怎么把 DSH 网页客户端配对到另一台设备上使用？
I want to access my DSH web session from another browser using a relay.
dsh-remote-control 的功能「远程配对」：从侧边栏控制面板启动主机到 relay 的连接并生成配对链接；用户可查看二维码或复制链接，在手机或其他浏览器打开 DSH 网页客户端。
dsh-remote-control 的功能「连接管理」：控制面板可保存 relay 地址和密钥、启停远程连接、定时刷新状态，并运行连接测试显示各步骤结果。
dsh-remote-control 使用前须知：远程浏览器的网页请求经你配置的 relay 转发到主机的本地 DSH Web 服务；relay 地址与共享密钥需由用户配置。

dsh-remote-control README · dsh-remote-control：Drive this DeepSeek Harness host from any browser — a phone, a tablet, another
desktop — and get **the real Harness client**, not a cut-down remote control.

dsh-remote-control README · dsh-remote-control：The plugin opens one outbound WebSocket to a relay and then does nothing clever:
the relay reverse-proxies the browser's HTTP and WebSocket traffic down that
socket, and the host replays it against its own loopback web server. The bytes
the remote browser sees are the bytes the local GUI sees. Sessions, approvals,
`ask_user` prompts, files, the terminal, settings, plugins, live token
streaming: all of it arrives by construction, and none of it needed a line of
code here.

dsh-remote-control README · dsh-remote-control：| Desktop browser | Phone — native reflow | Phone — "Fit" (desktop layout) |
|---|---|---|
|  |  |  |

dsh-remote-control README · Why proxying, and not a mobile UI：Earlier revisions of this plugin built a small mobile SPA and a method table
(`sessions.list`, `session.transcript`, `approval.respond`, …) behind it. Every
slice of the GUI it re-implemented was wrong in a new way: the sidebar did not
match, approvals arrived late, streaming text did not stream. A remote control
built from the outside is always a subset, and a subset is always out of date.
section: Why proxying, and not a mobile UI

text:
dsh-remote-control README · Why proxying, and not a mobile UI：Proxying the actual client retires that entire class of bug. The trade is that
the relay now terminates the browser's plaintext traffic instead of forwarding
opaque frames — see [Security](#security).
section: Why proxying, and not a mobile UI

text:
dsh-remote-control README · Install：**The plugin and the relay are one versioned pair.** Deploy them together: the
plugin calls `/_relay/*` and expects the tunnel framing in `PROTOCOL.md` §3, so a
new plugin against an old relay cannot register at all, and an old relay serves
its HTML shell for the paths the plugin asks for. `GET /healthz` reports the
relay's `version`, which is the fastest way to see a skew.

dsh-remote-control README · Install：```sh
pnpm install
pnpm check          # typecheck both halves, build, run 62 tests
scripts/install.sh  # pack, then print how to install dist/dsh-remote-control-<version>.tgz
```

Install the tarball through the plugin manager (sidebar → 插件) and restart.
Adding a bundle to a running profile always needs a restart, and reinstalling
the same version is a silent no-op — bump the version or remove the bundle
first.

dsh-remote-control README · The relay：Your machine dials **out** to a relay, and browsers reach your machine through
it — so you need one running somewhere both sides can reach. It is a
dependency-light Node program, and it ships inside this package under
[`relay/`](relay), with its own deployment guide:

```sh
cd relay && npm install --omit=dev
PORT=8080 PUBLIC_ORIGIN=http://relay.example node server.mjs
```

dsh-remote-control README · The relay：On a systemd host, `relay/install.sh` does the whole job — service account,
`/opt/dsh-relay`, dependencies, environment file, unit and start:

```sh
sudo ./relay/install.sh --public-origin https://relay.example
```

Then type that origin into the **Relay server** field at the top of the Remote
Control panel and press **Save**. That is all most people need.

dsh-remote-control README · The relay：**There is deliberately no default relay.** A relay is somebody's server, so
this plugin ships with none; until you name one, the panel says so rather than
dialling a stranger. Read [`relay/README.md`](relay/README.md) for TLS, upgrades,
the full environment reference and troubleshooting.

dsh-remote-control README · The Relay server setting：The field writes through the harness **settings service**, so the value lands in
your profile's `cordis.patch.yml` — the same user layer the app's own settings
pages write to — and is reapplied to this plugin at the next boot. Nothing is
stored twice: this plugin keeps no copy of its own, and the value it reads back
is the live config field the loader maintains.

Precedence, highest first:

dsh-remote-control README · The Relay server setting：| Source | Shown as | Editable in the panel |
|---|---|---|
| `DSH_REMOTE_RELAY` in the environment | *from DSH_REMOTE_RELAY* | no — the field is disabled |
| everything else | *saved to your profile* | yes |

The environment wins because it is a deployment's own instruction, and the field
is disabled rather than silently ignored when it is set.

dsh-remote-control README · The Relay server setting：There is deliberately no distinction between "saved from the panel" and "typed
into the profile patch": both are the same user layer of the same file, so a
panel that pretended otherwise would be inventing a state it cannot see. Type
the origin in whichever place you prefer — the panel is simply the one that
saves it for you.

Saving while the link is armed **restarts it against the new origin**
immediately, so the QR you are looking at is the one that works.

dsh-remote-control README · The Relay server setting：An origin is validated before it is stored: `http:` or `https:`, origin only, no
path. Anything else is refused with the reason, and the stored value is left
alone.

dsh-remote-control README · Test connection：When something is wrong the symptom is usually the same from the phone — an
offline page — while the cause can be any link in the chain. **Test connection**
walks it and names the one that broke:

dsh-remote-control README · Test connection：| Step | What it proves |
|---|---|
| Relay configured | an origin is set, and it is an http(s) origin |
| Relay reachable | the relay answers `/healthz`, and how fast |
| Versions match | the relay's reported version equals this plugin's — the skew that otherwise only shows up as a pairing page that will not finish |
| Host socket attached | this host actually holds a relay socket |
| Relay sees this session | the relay reports *this* session online, not just any host |
| Round trip through the tunnel | a frame goes host → relay → host through the real tunnel and comes back, timed |

dsh-remote-control README · Test connection：Steps that cannot run because an earlier one failed are reported as skipped
rather than red, so a single broken link does not read as six. The last step is
the one that matters most: an open socket can look healthy while frames are
going nowhere, and only a round trip proves otherwise.

dsh-remote-control README · If pairing does not get past the spinner：A pairing token is **single-use**, and the page that carried it keeps it in the
address bar. Reloading that page, or opening the link twice, therefore presents
a token the relay has already burned. The relay says so and the page offers
**Try another link** — mint a fresh one from the panel. Nothing needs
restarting, and no state is stuck.
section: If pairing does not get past the spinner

text:
dsh-remote-control README · If pairing does not get past the spinner：Two other dead ends are diagnosed on the page rather than left spinning: a relay
that answers with HTML instead of JSON (version skew) and a host that never
attaches (the plugin is not armed, or the Harness is not running). Both are
bounded — the pairing page never waits forever.
section: If pairing does not get past the spinner

text:
dsh-remote-control README · Use：The panel carries the installed version and the author credit beside its title —
`v0.9.7 Author: icrefin [icrefinai@gmail.com]` — the way the other plugins here
do.

**Start and Stop are the whole model.** Start opens an outbound connection to
the relay and pairs a browser to this host; Stop ends that pairing. Stopping is
also how a leaked link is revoked, so it does not pause — it finishes the
session, and browsers holding it must pair again.

dsh-remote-control README · Use：**A restart is not a Stop.** Restarting the app resumes the same session, so a
browser that is already paired keeps working; the identity is remembered for
exactly that reason, and the teardown that a reload, an upgrade or a shutdown
runs closes the socket *without* revoking the pairing. Without that, every
restart would silently cut off the browsers that were already paired, and the
first thing you would see is the relay's pairing page with nothing on screen to
explain it.

dsh-remote-control README · Where the relay secret lives：In its own file, `~/.dsh/relay-secret`, and **not** in the profile document. A
secret is a credential, not configuration: that document is rewritten by the
settings service whenever anything else in the row changes, it is the file an
operator opens to read their setup, and on this host it was already being
clobbered by a running build that did not know the field. The file is written
`0600`, holds nothing but the secret, and is read on every use — so a secret
corrected by hand or by a provisioning script takes effect at once, with no
restart.

dsh-remote-control README · Where the relay secret lives：The panel shows that file's contents — masked, with an eye to reveal it — so
the value in use can be read and corrected without leaving the app. There is no
environment variable for it: one was tried, and it silently outranked the panel,
so an edit in the UI could have no effect.

To give another host the same access, copy that one file:

```bash
scp ~/.dsh/relay-secret other-host:~/.dsh/relay-secret
```

dsh-remote-control README · Two lifetimes, and only one of them is short：| | Lifetime | Why |
|---|---|---|
| The **link** (the QR, `?t=…`) | 10 minutes, single use | It is a bearer credential in a URL. You may have screenshotted it, mailed it, or shown it across a room. Short and single-use means a leak is worth almost nothing a minute later. The panel re-mints one every time it is opened, so the QR on screen is always live. |
| The **pairing** (the browser's cookie) | a year | This is the thing that should persist. It survives restarting the app, updating it, and restarting the relay, because both the session and the browser's token are written down on the relay's side. |
section: Two lifetimes, and only one of them is short

text:
dsh-remote-control README · Two lifetimes, and only one of them is short：So a browser pairs **once**. It keeps working because the host resumes the same
session, which is why the host writes its identity down at all. The pairing is
only broken by a deliberate **Stop**, by the host losing its identity, or by the
relay dropping that browser's token because fifty other browsers paired while it
was idle — and in every one of those cases the browser is told which happened and
offered a fresh link, rather than left guessing.
section: Two lifetimes, and only one of them is short

text:
dsh-remote-control README · Two lifetimes, and only one of them is short：1. Open **Remote Control** in the Harness sidebar.
2. Press **Start**. The host connects out to the relay and a QR appears.
3. Scan it with a phone camera — or open the link in any browser.
4. The browser loads the Harness. That is the whole flow.

Stopping finishes the session rather than pausing it: the host tells the relay,
discards its own identity, and the old URL — and every browser holding a cookie
for it — is done. Starting again mints a fresh session and a fresh QR.
section: Two lifetimes, and only one of them is short

text:
dsh-remote-control README · Two lifetimes, and only one of them is short：**A restart is not a stop.** Restarting the app resumes the same session, so a
browser that is already paired keeps working — the identity is remembered for
exactly that reason. Only Stop, a pair the relay no longer recognises, or a
browser the relay had to drop when the session reached its limit, requires
pairing again.

To take a paired browser back out without touching the host,
`POST /_relay/unpair` clears its cookie.
section: Two lifetimes, and only one of them is short

text:
dsh-remote-control README · Remote display：The shipped client is built for a desktop viewport. It already collapses its
sidebar to a rail when it is narrow, so a phone is usable unaided — but three
things still needed fixing, and the host injects a small payload into the
tunnelled shell to fix them:

dsh-remote-control README · Remote display：| Concern | What the payload does |
|---|---|
| keyboard | `interactive-widget=resizes-content`, so a soft keyboard shrinks the layout instead of covering the composer |
| scaling | below 1120 px it offers **Fit** — the full desktop layout at the design width, fitted to the screen — and **Native**, the client's own reflow. The choice is remembered per device |
| gestures | `touch-action: manipulation` keeps pinch-zoom and drops double-tap zoom |

dsh-remote-control README · Remote display：The switcher is a `position: fixed` button that renders only below the design
width, and switching rewrites the viewport meta on the live document rather than
reloading, so an open conversation survives the change.

The payload is applied **only to tunnelled responses**. A browser running on the
host itself never sees it, which is why the local GUI is byte-identical to what
it was before this plugin was installed.

dsh-remote-control README · Routes：The `/api/dsh-remote-control` family is the operator's local control surface. Every
route is loopback-only, and the mutating ones require `POST`.

dsh-remote-control README · Routes：| Route | Method | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `/api/dsh-remote-control/status` | GET | phase, relay, pairing URL, tunnel counters |
| `/api/dsh-remote-control/start` | POST | arm the link, open the device socket |
| `/api/dsh-remote-control/stop` | POST | end the pairing: close the link, tell the relay, discard the identity |
| `/api/dsh-remote-control/pair` | POST | mint a fresh pairing token |
| `/api/dsh-remote-control/qr.svg` | GET | the pairing URL as an SVG QR |
| `/api/dsh-remote-control/settings` | POST | store the relay origin, and re-target a running link |
| `/api/dsh-remote-control/test` | POST | run the connection test and return its report |
| `/api/dsh-remote-control/trace` | GET | recent link traffic |

dsh-remote-control README · Routes：The panel asks for these routes **relative to the document** (`CLIENT_API`,
derived from `API` by `clientPath()` in `src/protocol.ts`); the route table above
stays absolute because that is what the web server matches. The distinction is
load-bearing here more than anywhere else: this plugin serves the web client at
`/s/<sessionId>/`, so an origin-absolute `/api/…` request from the panel's own
page leaves that scope and is answered by the relay's pairing page — a
`200 text/html` body, which the panel would report as `Unexpected token '<'`
rather than as an HTTP failure. `test/protocol.spec.ts` resolves both forms
against a tunnelled base to pin it.

dsh-remote-control README · Performance：A cold load of the client is ~12 MB of JavaScript. The tunnel keeps the origin's
compression for subresources, so that crosses the wire as ~6 MB; only a document
navigation drops `accept-encoding`, because the shell's HTML has to be readable
to splice in the display payload. Measured end to end through a public relay:
first paint at ~12 s cold, and the browser's own cache does the rest.

dsh-remote-control README · Security：**The harness credential never leaves the host.** The browser-session cookie the
Harness requires is minted *on the host*, bound to `127.0.0.1:<port>`, and
injected into the loopback replay. Neither the browser nor the relay ever sees
it, so a compromised relay cannot replay it against this machine's API.

dsh-remote-control README · Security：**The relay does see your traffic.** It terminates the browser's HTTP, so it can
read every request and response in plaintext unless you put TLS in front of it.
That is a real change from an opaque frame forwarder, and it is the price of
serving the real client through a relay. If it is not acceptable, run the relay
on a host you control, or terminate TLS at a reverse proxy you control. The
stored state is one JSON file (`hostSecret`, phone tokens, pairings), written
`0600`.

dsh-remote-control README · Environment overrides：| Variable | Effect |
|---|---|
| `DSH_REMOTE_RELAY` | relay origin the host dials; overrides the row's `relay` config |
| `DSH_HOME` | where the durable pairing identity is stored |

Relay-side: `PORT`, `HOST`, `STATE_FILE`, `WEB_ROOT`, `PUBLIC_ORIGIN`,
`PAIRING_TTL_MS`, `TUNNEL_HEAD_TIMEOUT_MS`, `TUNNEL_OPEN_TIMEOUT_MS`,
`BROWSER_IDLE_MS`, `DEBUG=1` (frame-level tracing).

dsh-remote-control README · Layout：```
src/
  index.ts                 host half: link, tunnel, cookie, routes
  protocol.ts              local panel contract, shared by both halves
  routes.ts                the /api/dsh-remote-control family + loopback fence

The published tarball carries `relay/` as well as `lib/`, so a relay can be stood
up from the same artifact that installed the plugin.

dsh-remote-control README · Versioning：The plugin and the relay are released from one repository and have to be able to
talk to each other, so they share a **compatibility line**: the first two digits
of the version. The rule is mechanical.

dsh-remote-control README · Versioning：| The change | Bump | Both sides? |
|---|---|---|
| Touches the relay, or the contract between the halves | **minor** — `0.9.x` → `0.10.0` | yes, both move together |
| Touches the plugin alone | **patch** — `0.9.1` → `0.9.2` | plugin only; the relay keeps its version |
| Touches the relay alone | **patch** | relay only; the plugin keeps its version |

dsh-remote-control README · Versioning：So any plugin on `0.9.*` works with any relay on `0.9.*`: `0.9.1`, `0.9.2` and
`0.9.9` are all the same line, and the connection test compares that line rather
than the whole version. A `major` bump means the halves are no longer expected to
interoperate at all.

`test/bundle.spec.ts` asserts the two package manifests agree on the line, so a
release cannot drift out of it by accident.

dsh-remote-control README · Verification：Four tiers, weakest to strongest:

```sh
pnpm check                  # typecheck, build, 62 unit + integration tests
node relay/verify.mjs       # 27 checks: the relay contract, no DSH needed
node relay/e2e.mjs --dsh http://127.0.0.1:19499 --token <from `dsh web`>
                            # 24 checks: real browser, real relay, real harness

dsh-remote-control README · Verification：1. **Unit** — the tunnel's header rewriting, cookie refresh, body streaming,
   injection idempotence, socket backlog and error paths, against a real
   loopback HTTP/WebSocket server.
2. **Integration** — `HostLink` against a **real relay process**: registration,
   the pairing cookie, tunnelled requests and bodies, `502` on host failure,
   `503` on a detached host, presence, identity persistence, and a clear error
   when the relay answers with HTML instead of its API.
3. **Contract** — `relay/verify.mjs` drives every route and upgrade the relay
   owns, with a stub host, so a failure is always the relay's.
4. **End to end** — `relay/e2e.mjs` pairs headless Chrome through a real relay
   against a running `dsh web`, then asserts what the page rendered at desktop
   width, at phone width, and after switching to Fit. It also re-opens a spent
   pairing link and requires a clear error step, because "the token was already
   used" must never look like "pairing is broken". It writes the three
   screenshots at the top of this file.

dsh-remote-control README · Verification：Tier 4 exists because tiers 1–3 can agree while the product is still broken: the
page has to actually render, and only a browser can say whether it did.

Two bugs found this way, both invisible to the lower tiers: the plugin resolved
`ctx.connection` at mount time and so never minted a cookie at all (the tunnel
returned `socket hang up`), and a retried request was rebuilt but never ended, so
it was constructed and never sent.

dsh-remote-control README · History：This plugin began as a ZCode-compatible client: it spoke Zhipu's relay protocol,
reproduced their HMAC handshake, and reimplemented the subset of the ZCode agent
RPC surface their phone page required. That work is preserved rather than
deleted, because the protocol archaeology is still accurate:

dsh-remote-control README · History：- [`scripts/phone-sim.mjs`](scripts/phone-sim.mjs) — drives ZCode's own phone page
  headlessly over the DevTools protocol, which is how their boot sequence was
  observed instead of guessed.
- [`docs/dsh-host-api-reference.md`](docs/dsh-host-api-reference.md) — the
  verified `ctx.*` surface a hand-built remote control needs. Superseded, and
  labelled as such, because the premise no longer holds.

dsh-remote-control README · History：The analysis behind that earlier design stays in the maintainer's notes; what
survived into this repository is the verified API reference above.

dsh-remote-control README · Provenance：Not affiliated with or endorsed by Zhipu. No ZCode code or protocol is used by
the current implementation.

dsh-remote-control README · Contributing：Issues and pull requests are welcome — see [CONTRIBUTING.md](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md)
for the development setup and the sign-off expectation. Please report security
issues privately as described in [SECURITY.md](.github/SECURITY.md).

dsh-remote-control README · dsh-remote-control：从任意浏览器——手机、平板、另一台桌面——驱动这台 DeepSeek Harness 主机，拿到的是
**真正的 Harness 客户端**，而不是一个被裁掉大半的遥控器。

插件向中继打开一条出站 WebSocket，此后不做任何取巧的事：中继把浏览器的 HTTP 与
WebSocket 流量反向代理到这条 socket 上，主机再把它重放到自己的回环 web 服务器。
远端浏览器看到的字节，就是本地 GUI 看到的字节。会话、审批、`ask_user` 提问、文件、
终端、设置、插件、token 流式输出：全由架构本身保证，本插件一行代码都没为它们写。

| 桌面浏览器 | 手机 —— 原生重排 | 手机 —— “Fit”（桌面布局） |
|---|---|---|
|  |  |  |

dsh-remote-control README · 为什么是反向代理，而不是移动端 UI：这个插件更早的版本自带一个小型移动端 SPA，后面挂着一张方法表（`sessions.list`、
`session.transcript`、`approval.respond`、…）。它重新实现的每一块 GUI，都以一种新的
方式出错：侧边栏对不上，审批来迟了，流式文本不流。从外部搭起来的遥控器注定是一个
子集，而子集注定会过时。

代理真实客户端，让这一整类缺陷直接退休。代价是：中继现在终结浏览器的明文流量，
而不是转发不透明的帧——见[安全](#安全)。
section: 为什么是反向代理，而不是移动端 UI

text:
dsh-remote-control README · 安装：**插件和中继是一对同版本发布的组件。** 请一起部署：插件调用 `/_relay/*`，并期待
`PROTOCOL.md` §3 里规定的隧道封装，所以新插件配旧中继根本注册不上，而旧中继会在
插件请求的路径上返回它自己的 HTML 外壳。`GET /healthz` 会报告中继的 `version`，
这是发现版本错位最快的办法。

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm check          # typecheck both halves, build, run 62 tests
scripts/install.sh  # pack, then print how to install dist/dsh-remote-control-<version>.tgz
```

通过插件管理器（侧边栏 → 插件）安装这个 tarball，然后重启。往正在运行的 profile 里
添加 bundle 总是需要重启；而重装同一个版本等于什么都没做——先把版本号往上提，或者
先把这个 bundle 移除。

dsh-remote-control README · 中继：你的机器向中继**出站**拨号，浏览器再经由中继抵达你的机器——所以你得在一个两边都能
到达的地方跑一个中继。它是个依赖很少的 Node 程序，就随本包发布在
[`relay/`](relay) 下，并带有自己的部署指南：

```sh
cd relay && npm install --omit=dev
PORT=8080 PUBLIC_ORIGIN=http://relay.example node server.mjs
```

在 systemd 主机上，`relay/install.sh` 一次做完所有事——服务账号、`/opt/dsh-relay`、
依赖、环境文件、unit 和启动：

```sh
sudo ./relay/install.sh --public-origin https://relay.example
```

然后把这个 origin 填进 Remote Control 面板顶部的 **Relay server** 字段，按
**Save**。大多数人到这一步就够了。

dsh-remote-control README · 中继：**这里刻意不设默认中继。** 中继是别人的服务器，所以本插件一个都不预置；在你指定
之前，面板只会说明这一点，而不会去拨一台陌生的机器。TLS、升级、完整的环境变量
参考与故障排查，见 [`relay/README.md`](relay/README.md)。

dsh-remote-control README · Relay server 设置：这个字段经由 harness 的 **settings service** 写入，所以值落在你 profile 的
`cordis.patch.yml` 里——也就是应用自己的设置页所写的同一个用户层——并在下次启动时
重新应用到本插件。没有任何东西存两份：本插件自己不留副本，它读回的值就是 loader
维护的那个实时配置字段。

优先级从高到低：

| 来源 | 显示为 | 面板中可编辑 |
|---|---|---|
| 环境里的 `DSH_REMOTE_RELAY` | *from DSH_REMOTE_RELAY* | 否 —— 字段被禁用 |
| 其他一切 | *saved to your profile* | 是 |

环境变量优先，因为它代表这次部署自己的指令；一旦设置了它，字段就被禁用，而不是被
悄悄忽略。

这里刻意不区分「从面板保存」和「直接写进 profile patch」：它们本来就是同一个文件的
同一个用户层，面板若假装有别，就等于凭空造出一个它看不见的状态。你愿意在哪写
origin 都行——面板只是那个替你保存的地方。

dsh-remote-control README · Relay server 设置：在链路已布防时保存，会立刻**用新 origin 重启它**，所以你眼前这个二维码就是能用
的那一个。

origin 在存储前会先校验：只接受 `http:` 或 `https:`，只允许 origin，不带路径。其他
一律拒绝并给出原因，已存的值保持原样。

dsh-remote-control README · 测试连接：出问题时，从手机上看症状通常都一样——一个离线页面——而原因可能是链条上的任何一环。
**Test connection** 会逐环走一遍，并指出断在哪一环：

| 步骤 | 它证明了什么 |
|---|---|
| 中继已配置 | 已设置 origin，且是 http(s) origin |
| 中继可达 | 中继能应答 `/healthz`，以及应答多快 |
| 版本一致 | 中继报告的版本与本插件相同——这种错位否则只会表现为一个永远走不完的配对页 |
| 主机 socket 已挂上 | 本主机确实持有一条中继 socket |
| 中继看得见本会话 | 中继报告在线的是*这个*会话，而不只是某台主机 |
| 经隧道的往返 | 一帧经由真实隧道走 host → relay → host 再回来，并计时 |

因为前面某一步失败而无法运行的步骤，会报成跳过而不是红色，所以一处断裂不会被读成
六处。最后一步最要紧：一条已打开的 socket 可以看上去很健康，而帧其实哪儿都没去，
只有往返才能证明不是这样。

dsh-remote-control README · 如果配对过不了转圈这一步：配对 token 是**一次性**的，而承载它的页面会把它留在地址栏里。因此刷新那个页面、或者
把链接打开两次，出示的就是中继已经烧掉的 token。中继会如实说明，页面则给出
**Try another link**——从面板上重新生成一个。什么都不用重启，也没有状态卡住。

另外两种死路会在页面上直接诊断出来，而不是让你看着它一直转：中继用 HTML 而不是
JSON 应答（版本错位），以及主机始终没有挂上（插件未布防，或者 Harness 没在运行）。
两者都有上界——配对页从不无限等待。
section: 如果配对过不了转圈这一步

text:
dsh-remote-control README · 使用：面板标题旁边带着已安装的版本和作者署名
（`v0.9.7 Author: icrefin [icrefinai@gmail.com]`），和这里的其他插件一样。

**Start 与 Stop 就是全部模型。** Start 向中继打开一条出站连接，并把一个浏览器配对到
本主机；Stop 结束这次配对。撤销一条泄漏的链接也是靠 Stop，所以它不是暂停——它把
会话了结，持有它的浏览器必须重新配对。

**重启不是 Stop。** 重启应用会续上同一个会话，所以已经配对的浏览器照样能用；身份被
记住，原因正在于此——而一次重载、升级或关停所执行的下线清理，关闭 socket 时**不**
吊销配对。否则每次重启都会悄悄切断已配对的浏览器，而你第一眼看到的会是中继的配对页，
屏幕上没有任何东西解释它。

dsh-remote-control README · 中继密钥放在哪里：放在它自己的文件里，`~/.dsh/relay-secret`，**不**在 profile 文档里。密钥是凭据，不是
配置：那份文档每次这一行里别的什么变动都会被 settings service 重写，它是运维人员
打开来读自己配置的那个文件，而且在这台主机上，它已经被一个根本不认识这个字段的
运行中构建覆写过。这个文件以 `0600` 写入，除密钥外不存别的东西，每次使用都重新读取
——所以无论手工改还是由置备脚本改，改完立刻生效，不用重启。

面板会显示这个文件的内容——打码，带一个眼睛图标可以揭开——所以在用的值可以直接读出
并改正，不必离开应用。它没有环境变量：曾经加过一个，结果它悄悄压过面板，于是 UI 里的
修改可能毫无效果。

要让另一台主机获得同样的访问权，把这一个文件拷过去：

```bash
scp ~/.dsh/relay-secret other-host:~/.dsh/relay-secret
```

dsh-remote-control README · 两种寿命，其中只有一种很短：面板上的倒计时很容易被误读，所以这里说准确些：

| | 寿命 | 原因 |
|---|---|---|
| **链接**（二维码，`?t=…`） | 10 分钟，一次性 | 它是装在 URL 里的 bearer 凭据。你可能截过图、发过邮件，或隔着房间展示过。短且一次性意味着，泄漏一分钟之后几乎一文不值。面板每次打开都会重新生成一条，所以屏幕上的二维码永远是活的。 |
| **配对**（浏览器的 cookie） | 一年 | 这才是应该持久的东西。重启应用、升级应用、重启中继都不影响它，因为会话和浏览器的 token 都记在中继那一侧。 |

所以一个浏览器只配对**一次**。它能一直用，是因为主机续上了同一个会话——主机把自己
的身份写下来，为的正是这个。配对只会被三种情况打断：一次刻意的 **Stop**、主机丢失
自己的身份，或者中继丢掉了那个浏览器的 token（因为在它闲着的这段时间里，又有五十个
别的浏览器配了对）——而无论哪一种，浏览器都会被告知发生了什么、并给出一条新链接，
而不是被丢在那里自己猜。
section: 两种寿命，其中只有一种很短

text:
dsh-remote-control README · 两种寿命，其中只有一种很短：1. 在 Harness 侧边栏打开 **Remote Control**。
2. 按 **Start**。主机向中继出站连接，然后出现一个二维码。
3. 用手机相机扫它——或者用任意浏览器打开这条链接。
4. 浏览器加载出 Harness。整个流程就这些。

Stop 是把会话了结，而不是暂停：主机通知中继、丢弃自己的身份，旧 URL——以及每一个
持有它 cookie 的浏览器——就此作废。再 Start 会生成一个新会话和一个新二维码。

**重启不是一次 Stop。** 重启应用会续上同一个会话，所以已经配对的浏览器照常能用——身份
被记住，为的正是这个。只有 Stop、中继不再认识的配对，或者会话达到上限时中继不得不
丢掉的浏览器，才需要重新配对。

要在不碰主机的情况下把一个已配对的浏览器摘掉，用 `POST /_relay/unpair` 清掉它的
cookie。
section: 两种寿命，其中只有一种很短

text:
dsh-remote-control README · 远端显示：随包发布的客户端是按桌面视口构建的。它在窗口变窄时本来就会把侧边栏收成一条窄栏，
所以手机上不加干预也能用——但仍有三件事需要修，主机往隧道里的外壳注入一小段
payload 来修它们：

| 问题 | payload 做了什么 |
|---|---|
| 键盘 | `interactive-widget=resizes-content`，软键盘于是压缩布局，而不是盖住输入框 |
| 缩放 | 低于 1120 px 时提供 **Fit**——按设计宽度铺开的完整桌面布局，缩放到屏幕上——以及 **Native**，即客户端自己的重排。选择按设备记住 |
| 手势 | `touch-action: manipulation` 保留双指缩放，去掉双击缩放 |

切换器是一个 `position: fixed` 按钮，只在设计宽度以下才渲染；切换时改的是当前文档
上的 viewport meta，而不是重新加载，所以进行中的对话能跨过这次切换。

dsh-remote-control README · 远端显示：这段 payload **只应用于经隧道返回的响应**。跑在主机本地的浏览器永远看不到它，正是
这个原因，让本地 GUI 与本插件安装之前逐字节相同。

dsh-remote-control README · 路由：| 路由 | 方法 | 用途 |
|---|---|---|
| `/api/dsh-remote-control/status` | GET | 阶段、中继、配对 URL、隧道计数 |
| `/api/dsh-remote-control/start` | POST | 布防链路，打开设备 socket |
| `/api/dsh-remote-control/stop` | POST | 结束配对：关闭链路、通知中继、丢弃身份 |
| `/api/dsh-remote-control/pair` | POST | 生成一个新的配对 token |
| `/api/dsh-remote-control/qr.svg` | GET | 配对 URL 的 SVG 二维码 |
| `/api/dsh-remote-control/settings` | POST | 存下中继 origin，并给运行中的链路换目标 |
| `/api/dsh-remote-control/test` | POST | 跑一次连接测试并返回报告 |
| `/api/dsh-remote-control/trace` | GET | 近期的链路流量 |

dsh-remote-control README · 路由：面板**相对文档**请求这些路由（`CLIENT_API`，由 `src/protocol.ts` 里的
`clientPath()` 从 `API` 派生）；上面的路由表保持绝对形式，因为 web 服务器匹配的就是
绝对路径。这个区别在这里比别处更要紧：本插件把 web 客户端伺服在
`/s/<sessionId>/` 下，所以从面板自己的页面发出一个 origin 绝对的 `/api/…` 请求，
就会离开这个作用域，由中继的配对页来应答——一个 `200 text/html` 响应体，面板会把它
报成 `Unexpected token '<'`，而不是一次 HTTP 失败。`test/protocol.spec.ts` 对着一个
隧道 base 解析这两种形式，把这个行为钉住。

dsh-remote-control README · 性能：客户端一次冷加载约 12 MB JavaScript。隧道对子资源保留 origin 的压缩，所以过线时约 6 MB；
只有文档导航会去掉 `accept-encoding`，因为外壳的 HTML 必须可读，才能把显示 payload
拼进去。经一个公网中继实测端到端：冷加载首绘约 12 s，剩下的交给浏览器自己的缓存。

dsh-remote-control README · 安全：**配对 URL 就是凭据。** 任何打开它的人都能抵达本主机。所以：

- 每条日志行里 URL 都打码（`hash=***`）；
- QR 路由和 status 路由都发 `cache-control: no-store`；
- 配对 token 一次性且会过期（默认 10 分钟）；
- 中继签发的浏览器 cookie 是 `HttpOnly`、`SameSite=Lax`，TLS 之后还带 `Secure`。

**harness 凭据从不离开主机。** Harness 要求的浏览器会话 cookie 是*在主机上*签发的，
绑定到 `127.0.0.1:<port>`，再注入回环重放。浏览器和中继都看不到它，所以即便中继被
攻陷，也无法拿它来重放本机的 API。

dsh-remote-control README · 安全：**中继确实看得到你的流量。** 它终结浏览器的 HTTP，所以只要没在它前面摆一层 TLS，它
就能读到每一个请求和响应的明文。相对一个只转发不透明帧的中继，这是实实在在的变化，
也是用中继伺服真实客户端所付的代价。如果这不能接受，就把中继跑在你自己控制的主机上，
或者在你控制的反向代理上终结 TLS。它存下的状态是一个 JSON 文件（`hostSecret`、手机
token、配对记录），以 `0600` 写入。

dsh-remote-control README · 环境变量覆盖：| 变量 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `DSH_REMOTE_RELAY` | 主机拨号的中继 origin；覆盖该行的 `relay` 配置 |
| `DSH_HOME` | 持久配对身份的存放位置 |

中继侧：`PORT`、`HOST`、`STATE_FILE`、`WEB_ROOT`、`PUBLIC_ORIGIN`、
`PAIRING_TTL_MS`、`TUNNEL_HEAD_TIMEOUT_MS`、`TUNNEL_OPEN_TIMEOUT_MS`、
`BROWSER_IDLE_MS`、`DEBUG=1`（帧级追踪）。

dsh-remote-control README · 目录结构：```
src/
  index.ts                 host half: link, tunnel, cookie, routes
  protocol.ts              local panel contract, shared by both halves
  routes.ts                the /api/dsh-remote-control family + loopback fence

发布的 tarball 同时带着 `relay/` 和 `lib/`，所以用安装插件的同一个 artifact 就能把
中继立起来。

dsh-remote-control README · 版本策略：插件和中继从同一个仓库发布，又必须能互相说话，所以它们共享一条**兼容线**：版本号的
前两位。规则是机械的。

| 改动 | 版本位 | 两边都动？ |
|---|---|---|
| 动到中继，或动到两半之间的契约 | **minor** —— `0.9.x` → `0.10.0` | 是，两边一起走 |
| 只动插件 | **patch** —— `0.9.1` → `0.9.2` | 只动插件；中继保留自己的版本 |
| 只动中继 | **patch** | 只动中继；插件保留自己的版本 |

于是任何 `0.9.*` 的插件都能配任何 `0.9.*` 的中继：`0.9.1`、`0.9.2` 和 `0.9.9` 都在
同一条线上，连接测试比较的也是这条线，而不是整个版本号。`major` 位一升，就意味着
两半不再预期能互操作。

`test/bundle.spec.ts` 断言两个包的 manifest 在同一条线上，所以一次发布不可能意外
漂出去。

dsh-remote-control README · 验证：四层，由弱到强：

```sh
pnpm check                  # typecheck, build, 62 unit + integration tests
node relay/verify.mjs       # 27 checks: the relay contract, no DSH needed
node relay/e2e.mjs --dsh http://127.0.0.1:19499 --token <from `dsh web`>
                            # 24 checks: real browser, real relay, real harness

dsh-remote-control README · 验证：1. **单元** —— 隧道的头部重写、cookie 刷新、响应体流式传输、注入幂等、socket 积压与
   错误路径，全部对着真实的回环 HTTP/WebSocket 服务器跑。
2. **集成** —— `HostLink` 对着一个**真实的中继进程**：注册、配对 cookie、经隧道的
   请求与响应体、主机故障时的 `502`、主机脱开时的 `503`、在线状态、身份持久化，以及
   中继用 HTML 而不是它的 API 应答时那个清楚的错误。
3. **契约** —— `relay/verify.mjs` 用一个桩主机把中继拥有的每条路由和每次 upgrade 都
   驱动一遍，所以失败必定是中继自己的。
4. **端到端** —— `relay/e2e.mjs` 让无头 Chrome 经由真实中继、对着一个运行中的
   `dsh web` 完成配对，然后断言页面在桌面宽度、手机宽度以及切到 Fit 之后各自渲染出
   了什么。它还会重开一条已用过的配对链接，并要求出现一个明确的报错步骤，因为
   “token 已经用过了”绝不能长得像“配对坏了”。本文件开头那三张截图就是它写下的。

dsh-remote-control README · 验证：第 4 层之所以存在，是因为 1–3 层可以全都同意，而产品依然是坏的：页面得真的渲染出来，
而只有浏览器能说它到底渲染了没有。

这样抓到的两个 bug 都躲过了更低的几层：插件在挂载时就解析了 `ctx.connection`，
于是一个 cookie 都没签发（隧道返回 `socket hang up`）；还有一个重试的请求被重建了
却从不结束，于是它被构造出来、却从没发出去。

dsh-remote-control README · 历史：这个插件最初是一个兼容 ZCode 的客户端：它讲智谱的中继协议，复刻了他们的 HMAC 握手，
又把他们手机页面所需的那一小块 ZCode agent RPC 接口重做了一遍。这些工作被保留而不是
删掉，因为那番协议考古至今依然准确：

- [`scripts/phone-sim.mjs`](scripts/phone-sim.mjs) —— 通过 DevTools 协议无头驱动
  ZCode 自己的手机页面；他们的启动序列就是这么被观察到的，而不是猜出来的。
- [`docs/dsh-host-api-reference.md`](docs/dsh-host-api-reference.md) —— 手搭一个
  遥控器所需的、经过验证的 `ctx.*` 面。已被取代，并如实标注为取代，因为前提不再
  成立。

那套早期设计背后的分析留在了维护者的笔记里；活进这个仓库的，是上面那份经过验证的
API 参考。
dsh-remote-control README · 出处：与智谱无隶属关系，也未获其背书。当前实现没有使用任何 ZCode 的代码或协议。

dsh-remote-control README · 贡献：欢迎提交 Issue 和 Pull Request——开发环境的搭建方式和 sign-off 要求见
[CONTRIBUTING.md](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md)。安全类问题请按
[SECURITY.md](.github/SECURITY.md) 所述私下报告。

dsh-remote-control README · 许可证：MIT —— 见 [LICENSE](./LICENSE)。

> 如果从手机驱动这台主机让你少跑了一趟桌前，一颗 ⭐ star 能帮更多 DSH 用户发现它。
